note: Three places a directive name was fabricated, each measured on 559 corpus files before the fix. D1: a directive naming an ATOM module WITH OPTIONS published the options as the module name - 15 references and 4 calls endpoints (references -> ':lists, as: R7Alias', kernel/alias_test.exs:17; calls -> ':lists, only: [append: 2].append', kernel/import_test.exs:86). D2: a TYPESPEC whose LEFT side names a function require/2, alias/1 or import/1 was read as a directive (references -> '[Path.t], require_opts', kernel/parallel_compiler.ex:278). D3: a DEFINITION HEAD named import was read as a directive (references -> '%Regex{re_pattern: re_pattern} = regex', regex.ex:296). The doc already claimed directives stay gated; no gate existed. Falsifier: mutant elixir/r7-directive-options-in-name, elixir/r7-spec-read-as-directive, elixir/r7-defhead-read-as-directive. D4 (added after the mutation A/B found a hole): a COMPUTED directive name (`alias Module.concat(A, B)`, `require Mod.Helpers.helper()`) publishes NOTHING - not the expression, not a prefix - so the option-text fallback cannot be reached by a readable argument either. The D2/D3 pins are stated twice, once with an UNREADABLE first argument and once with a STATICALLY READABLE one, because with only the unreadable form both the gate and the name extractor refuse and the fixture cannot tell which one did the work.
